claim_formal: ∀ finite alphabet Σ ∀ regular L⊆Σ*: generalized star height h_Σ(L) ≤ 3 (union, concatenation, complement in Σ*, star)

claim_formal: ∀^∞ n: every syntactically homogeneous ΣΠΣΠΣ circuit over a characteristic-0 field computing IMM_{n,n} has ≥ n^{√n/400} gates; and ∀ n≥2 such circuits of size ≤ n^{√n+4} exist (complexity n^{Θ(√n)})

quote_A.text: Thus the gate complexity over characteristic-zero fields is $`n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}`$.

quote_B.text: requires $`n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}`$ gates in homogeneous depth-five sum–product circuits

notes: Sharp up to the constant in the exponent, so M9 (M8 if only the lower bound is taken as headline). No explicit open problem: superpolynomial depth-5 bounds already followed from Limaye–Srinivasan–Tavenas; prior depth-5 IMM bounds needed bottom-support restrictions (Bera–Chakrabarti). Treated as a record (lower bound) pushed to the tight scale, P4/O1 by rule 7; O8 (strengthens known theorem) is a reasonable alternative. Lean DepthFive covers ℂ, char-0 fields and the upper bound.

quote_A.text: a deterministic polynomial-time reduction that transforms an End-of-Line instance of binary length N into a generalized circuit of total binary length $`N(\log N)^{O(1)}`$

notes: PCP-for-PPAD (BPR2016 Conjecture 2), quasilinear version. Constants exist but are not stated numerically, so no effective flag.

claim_formal: ∀ fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine M (unit moves, read-only heads, polylog-space accessor) ∃ deterministic simulator N, c, e ∀ input x ∀ binary cap T≥2 (access condition): N computes M's finite-control/halting outcome by time T in ≤ c·T^{2/5}·log^e T work-space bits

quote_A.text: its finite-control and halting outcome by time \(T\) can be computed deterministically in \(\softO(T^{2/5})\) work-space bits

quote_B.text: This improves the square-root space exponent for one-tape machines, answering Williams's question for this model.

notes: Williams (2025, Sec. 5) asked whether the one-tape √t space exponent can be lowered by a fixed constant; answered yes 'for this model' (supplied cap, accessor condition), so O5 is possible; P4/O7 (exponent record 1/2 → 2/5) is the rule-7 alternative. Lean OneTapeSpace 'capped' and 'unknown' theorems match.

claim_formal: ∃ uniform randomized word-RAM algorithm A ∀ Subset Sum instance (n≥2): A halts with correct answer w.p. ≥ 2/3, and ∀ c ∃ C_c, N_c: if n≥N_c and b≤n^c then every execution uses ≤ C_c·2^{0.49n} word operations

quote_A.text: every input with $n\ge N_c$ and $b\le n^c$ is processed, on every outcome of the random choices, in at most \[ C_c\,2^{0.49n} \] word operations

quote_B.text: A fixed reduction of the exponential rate below $1/2$ is a different objective from such polynomial-factor savings.

notes: Breaks the 2^{n/2} meet-in-the-middle exponent (Horowitz–Sahni) for worst-case Subset Sum; no explicit posed question is cited, so treated as a record (P4/O7); P2/O1 if 'can 2^{n/2} be beaten?' is counted as an open question. Companion: 2^{n/2}·poly time with O(2^{n/5}) words of space (space record improvement).

claim_formal: ∀ ε>0 ∃ C_ε ∀ d≥2: Q(d) ≤ C_ε·d^ε first-order queries suffice for TV ≤ 1/10 sampling of e^{−V}, I ⪯ ∇²V ⪯ 2I, known minimizer; and Q(d) ≥ c·log d for d≥d₀; hence γ* = 0

claim_formal: ∀ A>0 ∃ c_A, d_A ∀ d≥d_A ∀ M≤Ad² ∀ ε∈(0,1/10] ∀ one-pass M-bit-state learner on exact Gaussian measurements y_t=⟨x_t,S⟩, S uniform on S^{d−1}: P(angle(ŝ,S) ≤ ε) ≥ 2/3 → horizon T ≥ c_A·d·log(1/ε)

claim_formal: ∃ j ∀ instances: EATR (true sentences ∃x∈ℝ^r ∀y∈ℝ^s Φ(x,y), polynomials given by integer arithmetic circuits) ∈ C_jP; in particular ETR ∈ CH (∃ℝ ⊆ C_26P)

claim_formal: ∃ uniform deterministic algorithm A ∀ prime p (binary) ∀ nonzero dense f∈F_p[x] of degree n: A outputs the complete factorization (irreducible factors with multiplicities) in O(((n+1)⌈log₂ p⌉)^{10^{12}}) bit operations, without GRH or oracles

notes: Deterministic polynomial-time factorization over F_p (classically open; known under GRH only quasipolynomially, Evdokimov). Uses the uniform Hecke zero-free theorem from the companion OpenAI paper 'Primitive roots for every admissible integer base' (outside this family), hence the B flags. M8 is an alternative matrix.

claim_formal: ∀ d≥1 ∃ B(d)<∞ ∀ real planar polynomial vector field V of degree ≤ d: #limit cycles of V in ℝ² ≤ B(d)

quote_A.text: there is a finite nonnegative integer \(B(d)\) such that every real planar polynomial vector field of degree at most \(d\) has at most \(B(d)\) limit cycles in the whole plane.

quote_B.text: This establishes the uniform boundedness assertion in the second part of Hilbert's sixteenth problem.

notes: Hilbert's 16th (second part) asks for the maximum number and arrangement of limit cycles; only the finiteness of H(d) (uniform boundedness) is settled, with no effective B(d), so O5. Lean covers only the secondary result: quintic classical Liénard systems have at most 2 limit cycles, attained (degree-5 case of the Lins–de Melo–Pugh conjecture, M9). Hence 'different'.

Secondary results: singularity at reciprocals of every quartic Salem number in (1,2) and of a degree-31 non-Pisot root. quote_A.text: Thus Hadwiger's conjecture and its fractional-coloring weakening \(\chi_f(G)\le h(G)\) are false.

quote_A.text: Consequently, \[ 6\le \chi(\R^2)\le 7. \]

quote_B.text: We prove Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

notes: Erdős [Problem 4.33.6] (Erdős problems list), so P3; P1 if it is read as the named Erdős–Turán AP conjecture. The quantitative r_k bound is also new (quasipolynomial Szemerédi, a P4 record).
